FIXED in Stage 2 (Phase 24 adversarial review) — was UNKNOWN/no-match in Stage 1 because no record contained the word "Collection" as a distinct topic. AI-WF-002 (Create a New Event) genuinely explains the real Collection → Event → Components hierarchy (verified against onboarding screen 2's own text), but Stage 1/early-Stage-2 answerQuestion() only preferred a Workflow answer for HOW_TO/TROUBLESHOOTING question types — "What is a Collection?" classifies EXPLANATION, so it fell through to feature-only matching (zero features mention "Collection", hence UNKNOWN). Broadening the workflow-preference gate to include EXPLANATION (found via a different adversarial question, "What is a sync-slot?", which had the identical structural problem) fixed this as a side effect — a genuine improvement, not a loosened expectation.

gaps.note: Unchanged from Stage 1: ties at 100 across AI-FEAT-006/040/057; ascending-ID tiebreak happens to surface AI-FEAT-006, the most relevant of the three — a case where the tiebreak artifact does not cause a wrong answer. CHANGED 2026-08-17 (Phase 4.3, Decision 2, surface-size normalization) — by Phase 4.2 this tie had already shifted to AI-FEAT-006/AI-FEAT-017 at score 200 (a pre-existing drift from the Stage 1 composition described above, not caused by Phase 4.3). Phase 4.3 breaks that tie: primary is now AI-FEAT-006 confidently untied at "strong" (133.3 vs AI-FEAT-017's 115.2) — the same, correct record as before, just no longer hedged as a tie. capabilityStatus remains correctly AVAILABLE; matchQuality now mismatches the corpus's weak expectation only because the answer got more confident, not because it became wrong — a residual calibration/quality-tier effect of Decision 2, not a new governance intrusion.

Was "strong" in Stage 1 (AI-FEAT-033 alone at score 200). In Stage 2, the correct top match (AI-WF-004, Repair Missing or Incorrect Metadata, still correctly grounded in AI-FEAT-033) ties at score 300 with AI-WF-006 — a genuine, disclosed, hard limitation: AI-WF-006's own text legitimately contains the words "metadata"/"audit"/"repair" in a NEGATING context ("not Metadata, not Audit/Repair" — part of the Registry's own required four-way distinction). Pure keyword-overlap cannot distinguish a word appearing in a positive claim from a word appearing in an explicit exclusion. The primary match is still correctly AI-WF-004 (alphabetically first among the tie) and the answer is still correctly grounded and hedged — this is the system being appropriately conservative given a genuinely ambiguous lexical signal, not a wrong answer. A real candidate for smarter (still non-embedding) matching in a future stage, not a defect to patch here. CHANGED 2026-08-17 (Phase 4.3, Decision 2, surface-size normalization) — the AI-WF-004/AI-WF-006 tie described above is broken, but not by resolving the AI-WF-006 negation-context ambiguity; instead, normalization shifts the flat 300/300 tie apart and a different competitor, AI-FEAT-033 (Metadata Audit & Repair), becomes primary at a confident, untied "strong" (259.1) — AI-WF-004 drops out of the top 5 entirely. This is not an overstated full correction: it is a residual Feature-vs-Workflow near-tie, the same class already documented for V2's P17a case, not fixed in Phase 4.3 and not chased by tuning REF/damping. The current answer remains topically valid — AI-FEAT-033 is the genuinely correct feature for "repair missing metadata" — but it loses AI-WF-004's concrete step-by-step repair instructions, so this is a real, disclosed precision/completeness trade-off, not a clean fix of the original hard limitation.

FIXED in Stage 2 — Stage 1 could not resolve this because the boundary table's keyword phrasing was too narrow ("multiple users log in", not "multiple people log in with different roles"). A boundary-widening concept cluster (intentConcepts.js BOUNDARY_CONCEPT_CLUSTERS, "team-multi-role") now recognizes "different roles" as a paraphrase of the SAME already-evidenced multi-user-roles exclusion — same citation, wider recall, never a new unevidenced claim. This same fix ALSO caught and required repairing a genuine regression: a "team-collaboration" concept hint aimed at a different, legitimate paraphrase family ("several users... simultaneously") was, before a fix, strong enough to override this correctly-detected boundary — see AI-FEAT-058 Stage 2 Evolution Journal for the full account of why hint-boosted scores must never override a boundary, only raw-question scores may.
